finding_2_fifth_self_caught_defect.what_makes_it_different_from_the_first_f: The first four were wrong FACTS. This one was a wrong CORRECTION — it took a true value and three correct records and 'corrected' them into a false claim.
finding_2_fifth_self_caught_defect.the_false_sentence_quoted_exactly: at the commit where the prose says that bridge was governing the identity was b9272465dbe49f31
finding_2_fifth_self_caught_defect.where_it_lives: The commit message of 15c8b42, and the §BH6 prose transcribed by that same commit.
finding_2_fifth_self_caught_defect.immutability: The commit message of 15c8b42 is immutable history and is NOT rewritten. Per §BH7(b) the supersession lives in the register (§BH7(b)) and in commit U's prose and in this record.
finding_2_fifth_self_caught_defect.why_it_is_false: b9272465dbe49f31 is protocol_identity() at a47d24a — a true number read from the WRONG REGISTER. The quantity the identity bridge names is the DECLARATION identity, which is sha256 of the committed bytes of spreads_campaign_declaration.json, first 16 hex.

finding_2_fifth_self_caught_defect.none_of_them_says_protocol_identity: All three say 'identity bridge'. The only thing genuinely mislabelled was the launcher's prose and this executor's own draft, which called the value 'the protocol identity'. That was a NAMING error about a CORRECT value, not a wrong value.
finding_2_fifth_self_caught_defect.root_cause: A declaration identity and a protocol identity are both 16-hex sha256 prefixes and NEITHER CARRIES ITS NAMESPACE IN ITS OWN TEXT. Having correctly noticed that fd10bee04a2f9cbe was a record digest, the executor inferred it was therefore the wrong KIND of value — without reading line 46 of the declaration, which states in plain text that the declaration identity and that record's manifest digest are the SAME STRING BY CONSTRUCTION.
finding_2_fifth_self_caught_defect.why_the_existing_disciplines_did_not_cat: Every procedural discipline fired correctly and none of them could help. The gate was STOPPED rather than raced; superseded drafts were quoted rather than deleted; the finding was reported to the owner before being acted on. All of those govern HOW a correction is made. NONE of them tests WHETHER the finding is true.
finding_2_fifth_self_caught_defect.what_actually_caught_it: Implementation. The defect was caught only when the executor went to perform P1's first act and had to read line 34 to do so — at which point line 46 contradicted the finding outright. A FINDING THAT IS NEVER IMPLEMENTED IS NEVER TESTED. This one survived a full transcription, an owner ruling, and a landed commit without being contradicted.
finding_2_fifth_self_caught_defect.what_prevented_the_damage: §BH6(f) reading 3 left the three flagged sites untouched, on the restraint precedent set at §BH6(b): findings, not corrections, absent a fresh ruling. That restraint was adopted for an unrelated reason and it is the only thing that stopped three correct records from being overwritten with a false one. Restraint held under a WRONG PREMISE and still produced the RIGHT OUTCOME.
finding_2_fifth_self_caught_defect.what_it_would_have_cost: Had the executor acted on reading B, dfc98caf984055e3 — a protocol identity — would have been stamped into the declaration_identity field of P1's first act. begin_traced_queue takes that value as a parameter and its only check is falsiness, so NO GUARD ANYWHERE WOULD HAVE FIRED, and the bridge that six executed first acts depend on would have been silently broken.

finding_3_silent_acceptance_hole.ruling: §BH7(a) — recorded as a FINDING. Any guard is a SEPARATE PROPOSED BUILD and is not begun here or by implication.
finding_3_silent_acceptance_hole.defect: The identity is a caller-supplied parameter, never computed by the function. Its only validation is falsiness. Any non-empty 16-hex string passes, including a protocol identity, a record digest of an unrelated file, or a value from a stale commit.

finding_4_search_key_shape_false_negativ.class_disposition: EXISTING CLASS as of 5bb6f74 — filed as FIRINGS, not a mint, per the §BH5(a) limb that says a class already registered takes firings.
firings: A path-limited git command was issued with a git-root-relative pathspec from inside the pytest root. It returned EMPTY WITH EXIT 0 — 'not here' presented as 'clean'. Cause: a 'cd X && python ...' whose python was missing reported exit 1, and the executor read the failure as 'nothing happened' when the cd had already succeeded and moved the shell.

The §BC letter-collision search for 'BH7' was first run across all tracked paths and reported 460 matching files. Every hit was inside a binary or ASCII85-encoded artefact; a PDF's ASCII85 payload defeats git grep -I's binary detection. Re-run scoped to .md/.py/.json/.sh/.txt: 0 hits, with a negative control (§BH6 = 31 hits) proving the query had power.

The establishment table's rows were first sought under the guessed keys 'rows' and 'conditions'. Both are absent; the container is 'table'. The query returned 0 rows and a clean TOTAL of 0 rather than an error.

Blast radius was first tested with a bare grep for the word 'counts', which matched two files on an unrelated local variable and a docstring. The precise query — access to a counts KEY on this table — returns zero.
finding_4_search_key_shape_false_negativ.common_shape: In all four the ROOT or the KEY SHAPE was wrong and the result was clean, confident and false. None raised. Each was caught by re-running with a stated root and shape, or by a negative control.
